request: Scale the part 10x. Add drafts of 2 degrees to all vertical surfaces, with flat bottom surface as a hinge. Add rounds R=1mm to all inner edges and R=3mm to all outer edges. Exclude edges, inner or outer, on the flat bottom surface. Add two cylinder features with D=6mm and inner hole D=3mm. Cylinders should be spaced 30mm apart and shall be placed centered with respect to the main part. They should start on the flat bottom surface level and reach all the way to the part wall on the top side

actions.relational_constraint: Apply the same scale factor to the complete part
actions.unresolved_reference: The complete solid or body representing the part must be identified in the CAD model
steps: Select the complete single body SOLID 0, including the central curved cradle R01 and the perimeter support frame R02; do not scale individual faces independently.

Use the intersection of the symmetry planes x=0 and y=0 together with the existing CAD origin as the uniform scaling center so that the model remains symmetric and subsequent centered-feature coordinates remain stable.
Apply a uniform scale factor of 10.0 in X, Y, and Z. The reported 2.0 mm by 6.0 mm by 1.5 mm bounding box becomes 20.0 mm by 60.0 mm by 15.0 mm.
Confirm that the scaled extents are x=-10 to 10 mm, y=-30 to 30 mm, and z=-7.5 to 7.5 mm.

Confirm that FACE 11 remains the planar bottom mounting interface at z=-7.5 mm. The cylindrical seating face FACE 7 becomes radius 42.15 mm, and the concentric underside FACE 0 becomes radius 44.15 mm.
Treat the subsequently specified draft angle, 1 mm and 3 mm rounds, 6 mm cylinder diameter, 3 mm hole diameter, and 30 mm spacing as final post-scale dimensions; do not multiply those values by ten.

actions.relational_constraint: Use the flat bottom surface as the draft hinge
actions.unresolved_reference: The vertical surfaces, the flat bottom surface, the model direction defining vertical, and the required draft direction or sign must be resolved from the CAD model
steps: Use the model semantic orientation: +Z is the top, -Z is the bottom, and the vertical or mold-pull direction is parallel to CAD Z. The orientation confidence is 0.84, and FACE 11 is explicitly identified as the bottom mounting face.
Set the neutral or hinge plane to the plane of F007 / FACE 11 at scaled z=-7.5 mm. Preserve the intersections of the drafted walls with this bottom plane.
Select every planar wall whose original plane is parallel to Z: outer walls FACE 10, FACE 12, FACE 13, and FACE 14, and cavity-facing inner walls FACE 3, FACE 4, FACE 5, and FACE 6.

Apply a 2 degree neutral-plane draft in the +Z pull direction. Use a consistent material-removal sign: outer walls move inward above FACE 11 and inner cavity walls move outward above FACE 11, providing positive release toward +Z while leaving the bottom footprint fixed.
Do not draft horizontal faces FACE 1, FACE 2, FACE 8, FACE 9, or FACE 11. Do not classify the horizontal-axis cylindrical surfaces FACE 0 and FACE 7 as vertical planar walls.
Preserve mirror symmetry about x=0 and y=0 by applying identical draft magnitudes and opposite geometric offsets to each mirrored wall pair.
Recompute the B-rep after drafting because the original face indices identify the source topology and generated edge indices may change.

actions.target: all inner edges except inner edges on the flat bottom surface
actions.relational_constraint: Exclude any qualifying inner edge on the flat bottom surface
actions.unresolved_reference: The inner-edge classification and which edges are considered to be on the flat bottom surface must be determined from the CAD model
steps: Perform this operation after scaling and drafting but before creating the two new cylinders, so the round selection applies to the existing cradle and frame edges rather than to edges introduced by the new cylindrical features.
Because model.json does not provide brep_edges entries or EDGE indices, re-identify the post-draft edges by adjacent-face relationships and signed dihedral angle rather than inventing edge IDs.

Classify as inner edges all re-entrant or concave edges of the cradle and underside cavity. Candidate boundaries include the seating interface FACE 7 where it meets the end upper lands FACE 8 and FACE 9, and cavity boundaries involving underside FACE 0, underside lands FACE 1 and FACE 2, and inner walls FACE 3, FACE 4, FACE 5, and FACE 6.
Also include qualifying concave vertical cavity corners where the drafted inner longitudinal walls FACE 3 and FACE 4 meet the drafted inner end walls FACE 5 and FACE 6.

Exclude every edge belonging to the boundary wires of FACE 11, including both the outer perimeter and inner opening perimeter at z=-7.5 mm. An edge is excluded if it is geometrically incident to FACE 11, even if its other adjacent face is an inner wall.

Apply a constant-radius 1.0 mm rolling-ball fillet to the remaining concave edge set. Use tangent propagation only where it remains within the same intended concave chain and does not cross onto a FACE 11 boundary.

Validate that the fillets do not break the approximately 2.0 mm post-scale shell or rail thickness. If a selected chain cannot accept the requested radius, report the specific failed edge chain rather than silently reducing the 1.0 mm radius.
Confirm that the cylindrical seating function of F001 and the concentric shell relationship between FACE 7 and FACE 0 remain intact away from the rounded boundary transitions.

actions.target: all outer edges except outer edges on the flat bottom surface
actions.relational_constraint: Exclude any qualifying outer edge on the flat bottom surface
actions.unresolved_reference: The outer-edge classification and which edges are considered to be on the flat bottom surface must be determined from the CAD model
steps: Recompute the available edge set after the 1.0 mm inner rounds, because filleting can split or replace source edges.

Classify outer edges by convex signed dihedral angle. Include qualifying exterior vertical corner chains between the positive and negative X outer walls FACE 10 and FACE 12 and the positive and negative Y outer end walls FACE 13 and FACE 14.
Include qualifying convex upper exterior boundaries where the drafted outer walls meet the upper lands FACE 8 and FACE 9 or the exposed seating boundary FACE 7.
Do not include any edge incident to the bottom mounting face FACE 11. Keep both boundary wires of FACE 11 completely sharp and planar as required.
Apply constant-radius 3.0 mm fillets to the remaining convex edge chains. Prevent tangent-chain propagation from crossing onto excluded bottom edges.

Where inner and outer rounds approach one another in the scaled 2.0 mm-thick rail or shell regions, use a CAD-kernel corner solution that preserves the requested radii and solid validity. Do not reduce the requested 3.0 mm radius without reporting a geometric conflict.
Verify that all four lower outer footprint edges and all four lower inner-opening edges associated with FACE 11 remain unrounded.
Verify that mirror symmetry about x=0 and y=0 is maintained and that the planar mounting datum FACE 11 remains unchanged.

actions.relational_constraint: The two cylinders must be spaced 30 mm apart, centered with respect to the main part, start at the level of the flat bottom surface, and extend to the part wall on the top side
actions.unresolved_reference: The main-part center reference, cylinder axes and orientation, exact interpretation of the 30 mm spacing, flat bottom level, and top-side part wall that terminates each cylinder must be identified from the CAD model
steps: Create the cylindrical features after completing the scale, draft, and original-edge rounding operations.
Use the main-part symmetry planes x=0 and y=0 to define the feature pattern center. After scaling, the part is 20 mm wide in X and 60 mm long in Y.
Interpret the 30 mm spacing as center-to-center spacing. Place the centers along CAD Y because a 30 mm pair cannot fit within the 20 mm X width while remaining centered on the part.
Locate the cylinder axes at (x=0 mm, y=-15 mm) and (x=0 mm, y=15 mm). This produces a pair centered about x=0 and y=0 with exactly 30 mm center-to-center spacing.
Use axes parallel to +Z, consistent with the semantic bottom-to-top direction. Create the initial sketch on the XY datum plane coincident with the scaled bottom level of FACE 11 at z=-7.5 mm.

Sketch two circles of diameter 6.0 mm at the specified centers. The circles lie inside the projected 20 mm by 60 mm footprint, although their start locations are within the existing open underside rather than directly on the annular material of FACE 11.

Extrude each circular profile upward from z=-7.5 mm using an up-to-face or up-to-body end condition terminating at the top-side cradle wall F001 / FACE 7. At y=±15 mm the symmetric cylinders receive equal heights.
Allow each extrusion to pass through the underside cavity and intersect the curved shell at FACE 0, then fuse it with SOLID 0 so that each post is structurally joined to the central cradle wall.

Trim the upper ends to the concave seating surface FACE 7 rather than using a blind common height. The resulting top boundaries must conform to the curved top wall and must not protrude into the functional seating space.

Maintain two identical, mirror-symmetric cylindrical bosses and verify that the final result remains a valid single solid. If contact only at the terminal face produces a non-manifold condition, extend the cylinders slightly into the shell before the Boolean union and trim the result back to FACE 7.

actions.operation: Create an inner hole in each cylindrical feature
actions.target: the two newly created cylindrical features
actions.relational_constraint: Place one inner hole within each cylinder
actions.unresolved_reference: The hole-axis alignment and the depth or end condition of each hole are not explicitly stated and must be resolved before modeling
target face code: new cylindrical feature at x=0, y=-15
new cylindrical feature at x=0, y=15
steps: Use the same two cylinder center points, (0,-15) mm and (0,15) mm, and constrain each hole axis to be concentric with its corresponding 6.0 mm outer cylinder and parallel to +Z.
On the bottom-level XY sketch plane at z=-7.5 mm, draw one 3.0 mm diameter circle at each cylinder center.
Cut each hole through its full corresponding cylinder, using an up-to-face end condition at F001 / FACE 7 or an equivalent through-all cut limited to the boss and intersected top wall.

The full-depth interpretation is preferred because the request describes an inner hole in each cylinder without specifying a blind depth. This produces an annular cylinder with 1.5 mm radial wall thickness.
Ensure that each cut opens at the bottom level and reaches the curved top-side wall, producing a coaxial opening through the boss. Do not offset the holes relative to the outer cylinders.
Verify both holes are diameter 3.0 mm, both outer cylinders remain diameter 6.0 mm, and the cylinder center spacing remains 30.0 mm after the Boolean cuts.
Check the final solid for valid topology, adequate residual material at the boss-to-shell junction, preserved symmetry, and no unintended modification of the excluded bottom-face edge rounds.
